newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia, Japan in new air capacity deal.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia, Japan in new air capacity deal.

text.p: The Australian government said on Monday it had reached an agreement to lift Australia's air services capacity to Japan.
Under the agreement with the Japanese government, Australia will add four Boeing 767, or alternatively two Boeing 747, services out of Osaka.
It also gained an additional frequency at Fukuoka.
"This is the first increase in capacity in more than two years and will create jobs for Australians," Transport Minister John Sharp said in a statement.
Sharp said Ansett Australia had sought the additional capacity to move to daily services at Osaka and it would now apply to the International Air Services Commission to take up the new capacity.

He said Qantas Airways Ltd had indicated to the government it wanted to put on a fifth frequency into Fukuoka within its existing capacity entitlements, but needed approval to operate an additional service into slot-constrained Fukuoka.
"This increase in capacity will enhance air services and improve the competitive position of Australia's carriers in our most important tourist source market," he said.
Under the agreement, two of the additional Boeing 767 services would become available from March next year, with a further two services available from October next year.
